plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE + GSEA (no replicates)
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile confirms a 1-vs-1 design (1 treated liver sample vs 1 control liver sample, no biological replication) from salmon-derived raw gene counts (12000 genes x 3 columns incl. gene symbol, human). With no within-group replicates, DESeq2/edgeR cannot estimate dispersion, so per the grounded procedure (rule R-0003) no inferential p-value has statistical validity here. The plan therefore: (1) runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, library sizes) to characterize the two samples before any modeling; (2) filters low-count genes and computes DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors purely for normalization (no dispersion/test fitting); (3) reports normalized counts and descriptive log2 fold changes (treated vs control) explicitly labeled as non-inferential, with no adjusted p-values; (4) uses these descriptive fold changes to rank the full gene list for preranked GSEA (fgsea) against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary), both staged locally for human, again treated as descriptive/hypothesis-generating since the design supports no significance test; (5) produces a final report stating explicitly that this design cannot support inferential DE calls and naming the replicated design that would.
